Iodine in the Human Diet The shiny purple-black crystals of elemental iodine were first prepared in 1811 from the ashes of seaweed. Several species of seaweed concentrate the iodine that is pre­sent in low proportions in seawater, and for many years, seaweed was the major practical source of this element. Most iodine is now produced from natural brines via oxidation of iodide ion with chlorine.
